description: Bounded local PostgreSQL and MinIO checkpoint for deletion-worker interruption recovery. It simulates a worker process disappearing after claiming a deletion lease without Release/Complete, including one account whose object versions were already erased while its database ledger remained intact. After lease expiry, a replacement worker must reclaim both accounts and converge idempotently without resurrection.

interruptionCases.description: lease claimed and then abandoned before object or database erasure
lease claimed, real uploaded object versions erased, database object ledger intentionally retained, then process simulated as disappeared without Release/Complete

requiredSequence: create and fence two synthetic accounts at deletion epoch 2
upload at least one real versioned MinIO object for each account and retain canonical database object ledger
claim both deletion leases directly without invoking Worker.Sweep
for case claimed-before-erasure perform no erasure and abandon the lease
for case object-erased-before-db-sweep erase the real object version with the database object ledger intentionally retained and account state still deleting, then abandon the lease
do not call Release, Sweep or Complete for either abandoned claim
prove replacement worker cannot claim before lease expiry
wait only until the bounded one-second lease expires
object erasure remains idempotent for the already-erased case because the ledger survives
replacement worker completes database sweep and tombstone transition for both accounts
final deletion backlog pending and stuck counts are zero
all account-owned database rows are zero and no uploaded object version is resurrected
abortCriteria: an abandoned lease is reclaimable before its expiry
the replacement worker cannot reclaim both expired leases
already-erased object handling creates a new version or resurrects data
database object ledger is removed before replacement-worker convergence in the partial-erasure case
replacement worker reports an erasure error
any account-owned row or uploaded object version survives final convergence
result contains account id, object key, database URL, signed URL, token or credential
limitations: lease abandonment is a deterministic process-interruption simulation, not an operating-system SIGKILL or host crash
one-second lease is a bounded test configuration and not a production lease recommendation
two accounts and one replacement worker do not establish deletion throughput or capacity
local PostgreSQL 16 and MinIO are not production-equivalent dependencies
